author: Andrew Wilson Sports Writer
title: Morgantown punches ticket to Class AAAA state championship game | West Virginia High School Sports | wvnews.com
text:
SOUTH CHARLESTON, W.Va. — For the first time in program history, the Morgantown softball team punched its ticket to the state championship game.
The Mohigans punched their ticket to the Class AAAA championship game with their 6-0 victory over George Washington at the WVSSAC State Softball Championships on Wednesday at Little Creek Park in South Charleston.
Scoreless until the fifth inning, the scoreless tie was broken in the top of the fifth as Carper Messerly tripled to right field and scored on Kayleigh White’s RBI groundout.
Morgantown threatened in the top of the sixth as Caraline Mallow reached on an error and Grace Robinson hit a fly ball that narrowly touched down in fair territory in left field. A single by Madi Stone loaded the bases.
Then, Robinson hit a 1-1 pitch right up the middle for a two-run single.
Morgantown added to its lead in the top of the seventh on Grace Robinson’s bases-loaded walk, then Beth Robinson’s RBI groundout and when Grace Robinson scored on a passed ball.
The Class AAAA state championship game is at 1:30 p.m. Thursday at the same location.
MORGANTOWN 3, Cabell Midland 0: Madison Wisman pitched a complete-game one hitter and struck out six batters in the Mohigans’ victory.
She also was impactful at the plate as she was 1-for-2 with a double, sac fly and one RBI.
Karlee Salmoms got the lone hit for the Knights.
For the Mohigans, Madi Stone was 2-for-3 with an RBI, accounting for two of the Mohigans’ three hits on the afternoon.
Drea Watts took the loss in the circle despite only allowing three runs on three hits while striking out 12 batters.
Wisman’s sac fly in the top of the third got the Mohigans on the board, and in the top of the seventh, Morgantown increased its lead on an RBI groundout from Stone and with Robinson scoring on a throwing error.
GEORGE WASHINGTON 1, University 0: Kacie Long’s RBI single in the top of the seventh was the difference as the Patriots got the win.
University threatened in the bottom of the seventh, but with a runner on third, a bunt attempt was caught by George Washington pitcher Kynzi Bellamy, who immediately threw to third base.
The throw got by the third baseman, prompting Carley Voithofer to take off for home. But the throw home was in time, and Voithofer was tagged out.
Sophia Lehosit took the loss in the circle despite carrying her perfect streak of not allowing any base runners from the previous game into the first four innings of the University game.
The streak lasted 13 innings and was broken up by Ava Armstrong, who hit the first pitch she saw to left field for a single. In the end, it was one of four hits she allowed on the afternoon. She struck out six batters.
For the Hawks, Maddie Campbell finished 2-for-4 while Maddie Shaver was 2-for-3. Voithofer was 1-for-3 while Whitney Cox finished 1-for-2.
UNIVERSITY 1, Hurricane 0: Maddie Campbell did a little bit of everything as she led off with a triple and scored on Maddie Shaver’s RBI groundout.
That was all the run support that Campbell needed as she pitched a complete-game three-hitter and struck out eight batters. She didn’t issue any walks, either.
At the plate, Campbell accounted for two of the Hawks’ four hits herself. Lexi Elza was 1-for-3 while Sophia Lehosit finished 1-for-3.
The Redskins, however, threatened in the top of the seventh as Layla Hodges doubled down the left-field line and Hadley Lawson hit a 1-1 pitch into center field for a single, and a wild pitch moved each runner up one base with only one out.
But Campbell struck out the next two batters to escape the threat and keep the Hawks alive in the tournament.
For Hurricane, Josie Shamblin, Lawson and Hodges were each 1-for-3.
PARKERSBURG SOUTH 3, Cabell Midland 0: Anniston Shelton did a little bit of everything, both in the circle and at the plate.
In the top of the first inning, after Abbie Corbin singled, Anniston Shelton crushed a two-run homer over the fence in left field.
While the Patriots would score again, that would be all of the run support that Shelton would need as she pitched a complete-game one-hit shutout. She struck out 11 batters and didn’t issue any walks.
Leading 2-0, an RBI single by Bryleigh Pickens extended the Patriots’ lead to 3-0 in the fourth inning.
Becca Conrad got the lone hit for the Knights; she finished 1-for-3.
The University-Parkersburg South game ended too late for press time.
